item.text: {"cases":[{"case_id":"R01","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"When polling returns an older revision for an existing job, on_poll unconditionally applies it, replacing newer state and violating the revision contract.","locations":["poll.py:2","store.py:2"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Apply the same per-job revision guard used by on_live, or centralize that guard in apply for both sources.","verification":"Deliver a newer live event followed by an older poll event for the same job; verify the newer state remains and a subsequent newer poll event is accepted."}]},{"case_id":"R02","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R03","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R04","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"Calls through request still pass milliseconds directly to the provider, which now interprets that value as seconds; effective timeouts become 1,000 times the public argument's intended duration.","locations":["client.py:2","provider.py:2"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Preserve request's timeout_ms argument and convert it to seconds before calling provider.send.","verification":"Call request with timeout_ms=1500 and verify transport.send receives timeout=1.5."}]},{"case_id":"R05","coverage":"complete","findings":[]},{"case_id":"R06","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F-ready","cause":"After start became async, launch calls it without awaiting it, so initialization does not complete before ready is published. The prior closure premise that start completed synchronously no longer holds.","locations":["owner.py:2","owner.py:3","handler.py:1"],"severity":"high","origin":"introduced","disposition":"reopened","suggested_change":"Await handler.start() before publishing ready, allowing initialization failures to propagate without publishing readiness.","verification":"Suspend initialization and verify ready is absent until initialization completes; make initialization fail and verify ready is never published."}]},{"case_id":"R07","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"Each outer retry generates a new key and ignores operation_id. A successful checkout whose response is lost can therefore be repeated under a different key, including across checkout invocations, defeating provider deduplication.","locations":["checkout.py:4"],"severity":"high","origin":"unknown","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Use the caller-supplied operation_id as the provider key for every attempt and every invocation of the same logical checkout.","verification":"Simulate a committed operation with a lost response, then retry within and across checkout invocations; verify every send uses operation_id and only one logical operation commits."},{"id":"F2","cause":"Both checkout and gateway own retry loops, allowing up to three provider sends per outer iteration and exceeding the supplied max_attempts upper bound.","locations":["checkout.py:2","gateway.py:2"],"severity":"medium","origin":"unknown","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Keep retry ownership in checkout and make gateway perform one provider.send per call, so max_attempts bounds all sends.","verification":"Make every send time out with ample deadline budget and max_attempts=2; verify exactly two sends occur."},{"id":"F3","cause":"Every provider send receives the original duration budget, without subtracting elapsed time or checking exhaustion. Multiple attempts can therefore run beyond the total deadline measured from checkout entry.","locations":["checkout.py:4","gateway.py:4"],"severity":"high","origin":"unknown","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Compute a monotonic expiration at checkout entry, check remaining time before each attempt, and pass only the remaining duration to the single-attempt gateway. Stop when the budget is exhausted.","verification":"Use a controlled clock and timed failures to verify subsequent timeouts decrease by elapsed time, no attempt starts after expiration, and total waiting stays within the supplied budget."}]},{"case_id":"R08","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"The new audit handler is never registered: build constructs App with an empty handler list, so running the built application invokes audit zero times instead of exactly once.","locations":["bootstrap.py:3","app.py:4","audit.py:1"],"severity":"medium","origin":"introduced","disposition":"open","suggested_change":"Import audit.handle in bootstrap and register it exactly once in the handlers passed to App.","verification":"Build the application and run one event; verify audit_store receives exactly one matching entry."}]},{"case_id":"R09","coverage":"complete","findings":[{"id":"F1","cause":"A non-owner can call read_doc and receive doc.body because the function never checks ownership.
